excerpt: FOHENAGH WIN The Fohenagh Junior “A” hurlers kept their championship hopes alive when they defeated Ballygar 0-11 to 0-9 in a hard fought game at Ahascragh on Saturday evening last. The first half was closely contested and the sides finished level 0-5 each with goal opportunities missed by both sides. Ballygar forged ahead to lead 0-9 to 0-7 but the Fohenagh side scored the last four points to run out deserving winners. Fohenagh still hope for a Sarsfields victory over Ballygar to stay in the race. They were best served by Noel Higgins (in goal), backs, Michael Barrett, Colm Kirwan and the Leonard brothers, Padraic and Niall, Raymond Higgins and Jimmy Devine (until injured) at midfield and forwards, John Devine, Alan Mockler, Garry Lohan and free taker, Alan Madden. The Ballygar side were best served by Pat Quinn, Tom Feeney, Frank Harkin (in goal), Paddy Flynn, Eamonn Larkin and Tomás Kilcommins.

caption: INA snip — Connacht Tribune 2 Nov 1984: Vital For St. Thomas — St. Thomas 2-1 Fohenagh 1-1 in the Under-12 "C" final of the Coiste Iomana Tournament at Loughrea; Sean Moclair named for heroic defending and among the best for Fohenagh
excerpt: Vital For St. Thomas … After a fine first half showing in this Under-12 "C" final in the Coiste Iomana Tournament in Loughrea on Monday, St. Thomas held out for a win. They were awarded a 21-yard free after four minutes and full-back Tony Headd slammed home a goal. In the ninth minute St. Thomas got another free and full-back Headd obliged again with a point. The first real attack by Fohenagh was defied by a great score from Kenneth Larkin. St. Thomas attacked again and Enda McGarry ended it with a great goal to leave St. Thomas leading by 2-1 to 0-0. But for some heroic defending by Sean Moclair they would have stretched their lead even further early in the second half. Fohenagh were at last rewarded when Paul Kennedy got a point after nine minutes of the second half. They picked up their game very much after this and a goal by John Devine brought them closer to St. Thomas after ten minutes of the second half. But they could not get through for the all-important goal. St. Thomas can thank in particular Tony Headd, Sean Fahey, David Quinn, Kevin Smyth, and Justin Flannery. Best for Fohenagh were Noel Higgins, Sean Moclair, Eric Lally and Tony Kirwin. St. Thomas: K. Larkin, S. Fahey, T. Headd, D. Quinn, K. Smith, D. Fitzgerald, M. Headd, J. Flannery, A. Rowland, O. excerpt: Ahascragh come good in second half to secure U-21 final place … BY J. B. DONOHOE WHILE Ahascragh and Fohenagh are next-door neighbours from the far-flung frontier of Galway hurling on the field of play there is no love lost between them. That was patently obvious to the hardy band of rival supporters who braved the deep freeze at St. Brendan's Park, Loughrea, on Sunday to witness the replay of the semi-final of the U-21 ‘C’ Hurling Championship. One week earlier at Duggan Park, Ballinasloe, the sides drew 2-4 each and it was perhaps scarcely surprising that the players were getting somewhat fed up of their rivals, as Sunday's was the fourth clash between them this year. … FOHENAGH: M. caption: INA snip — Connacht Tribune 13 Sep 1991: A Workmanlike win for Salthill juniors in county semi — Salthill 2-8 Fohenagh 1-7 in the county junior championship quarter final at Athenry (headline says semi); Tony Kirwan goal for Fohenagh
excerpt: A Workmanlike win for Salthill juniors in county semi … THE Salthill hurling team, newly promoted to Junior 'A' status only this season, underlined its potential with a clear, if workmanlike, four point victory over Fohenagh in this county championship quarter final clash at Athenry on Sunday. … A well struck free from Ryan, that went all the way to the net, established a three point lead for Salthill, with only the accuracy of Fohenagh's free taker Gerry Burke — himself a former Salthill player — keeping his side within striking distance against a rearguard in which the reliable full back triumvirate of Joe Greaney, Denis O'Mahoney, and John McGrath were outstanding. Salthill could have found themselves in all kinds of trouble after the resumption when a speculative shot from Tony Kirwan went past Salthill goalkeeper Stephen Cullinane, to narrow the gap to just a point. However, points by Ryan, McGee, and a well-taken Michael Gavin goal midway through the half re-established Salthill's lead. … Full back Micheal Barrett, centre back Colm Kirwan — the team's best player — Seamus Lohan and the evergreen Eugene Hession tried hardest for Fohenagh.

caption: INA snip — Connacht Tribune 5 Nov 1993: Athenry's perfect blend helps secure Junior A hurling title — Athenry 1-8 Fohenagh 0-9 in the county Junior A hurling final at Duggan Park, Ballinasloe; Fohenagh team includes S. Mochlair, T. Kirwan (0-2), John Devine and A. Madden (0-5, all frees); VANQUISHED team photo names Tony Kirwan, Padraig Leonard, John Devine, Alan Madden and Seamus Mocklair. S. Mochlair / Seamus Mocklair (print) = Séamus Moclair; Padraig Leonard (print) = Pádraic Leonard
excerpt: VANQUISHED ... the Fohenagh side which failed in their bid to win the county junior title for the first time in history when they were defeated by Athenry in the final at Ballinasloe on Sunday. Back row, left to right: Tony Kirwan, Michael Barrett, Gerry Madden, Padraig Leonard, Joe Fallon, Gerry Burke, Seamus Lohan and Padraig Daly. Front row: John Devine, Alan Madden, Colin Kirwan, Noel Higgins, Paul Kennedy, Seamus Mocklair and Michael Coen, Team mascot Daniel Lyons. … Athenry's perfect blend helps secure Junior A hurling title Athenry 1-8 Fohenagh 0-9 by John Fallon BEFORE a ball was ever pucked in this year's junior A hurling championship Athenry, with their blend of experience and youth, were installed as firm favourites for the title. They lived up to that billing at Duggan Park, Ballinasloe, on Sunday but only after they fought off a dogged battle from a Fohenagh side who refused to surrender the chance of their first smidgen of glory since their famous County Cup wins of '59 and '60. Victory would have crowned a great year for Fohenagh. They packed in training after they lost their first two games in this year's championship but got back into the title race with victory in a group play-off which saw them twice beat Salthill. The exploits of Tony Kirwan for the victorious Galway U21 side — and his subsequent elevation onto the senior side — provided a great boost to Fohenagh and they showed great spirit when lowering Castlegar in the semi-finals. But on Sunday they were beaten by the better team with Athenry's experience in crucial positions, coupled with the containment of Kirwan until the closing stages by captain Michael Higgins, proving decisive in an open game of hurling which provided plenty of entertainment for the relatively large crowd. … Fohenagh full-back Colin Kirwan led as a captain should while wing-backs Michael Coen and Gerry Madden had some great moments. Padraig Leonard and Padraig Daly hurled well around the middle of the field but they were unable to stop Declan Higgins' dominance of this area. The containment of Tony Kirwan robbed Fohenagh of their most dangerous forward and while Seamus Lohan, John Devine and Alan Madden threathened with sporadic forays, it was not with the same sort of dash that Kirwan has led the Fohenagh attack all season. … Fohenagh: N. Higgins, P. Kennedy, C. Kirwan, S. Mochlair, M. Coen, M. Barrett, G. Madden, P. Leonard, P. Daly (0-1), T. Kirwan (0-2), S. Lohan (0-1), John Devine, G. Burke, J. Fallon, A. Madden (0-5, all frees). Subs: Jimmy Devine for Fallon, 34 mins; N. Leonard for Coen, inj. 39 mins. Referee: Michael Hedderman.
